The value below is the exact vm.rollFork value at the block timestamp; sGHO yield accrues per second, so a live dev anvil reads marginally higher as it advances block.timestamp while mining.

holders.label: REAL_HOLDER
notes: Large real sGHO holder (~4.59M GHO). Single Supplied leg.
Share count is identical at 25_230_126 and 25_287_877 (holder hasn't moved) — the GHO delta between the two pins is pure accrued savings yield.

ground_truth.method: vault convertToAssets + redeem-100% round-trip (NOT a Python re-derivation)
ground_truth.detail: Two independent checks pin the value. (1) No over-reporting: the synthetic suite deposits a known amount, redeems 100% of the shares, and asserts the GHO actually received ~= the oracle-reported amount -> proves convertToAssets carries no exit fee / cooldown / withdrawal haircut. (2) Exact real value: oracle.getOracleBalanceForAsset == sGHO.convertToAssets(holder shares) at the pinned block, with the share balance also pinned. Plus protocolId == erc4626, positionId == abi.encode(wrapper), PositionKind.Supplied.

aave_ui_reconciliation: Aave's 'Savings GHO (sGHO)' tile shows the sGHO share count (~4.58M); the withdraw preview shows redeemable GHO (~4.59M). The adapter reports the latter (convertToAssets), matching 'you'll receive 4.59M GHO'. The ~0.29% gap between the two is accrued savings yield, not an error.
